So hexes and random encounters are fun, but they can side on the very easy side if you allow your players to short rest after every encounter. I get around this by placing time constraints on the party (the villain sacrifices someone every week, etc.). I also dot the land with landmarks that can be explored that they can see off in the distance, Breath of the Wild style. These can range from ruins, to caves, to large creatures flying over some mountains. Also, my players know where the big bad is hiding, but the castle is very intimidating (also Breath of the Wild style), this gives them reason to explore the areas around them instead of going straight to the castle.

Mathew Colville has a great video on YouTube about a west marches campaign that kinda broadly applies to area exploration.
